description: Octavian becomes Augustus, establishing the Roman Empire after the fall of the Republic
Maximum territorial extent under Emperor Trajan, spanning from Britain to Mesopotamia
Diocletian divides the empire into Eastern and Western administrative units
Permanent division into Western and Eastern Roman Empires
Fall of the Western Roman Empire when Odoacer deposes the last emperor
Sargon unifies Mesopotamia, creating the first known empire in history
Empire reaches peak under Naram-Sin who declares himself god-king
Collapse under Gutian invasions and internal rebellion
Temüjin unites Mongol tribes and is proclaimed Genghis Khan
Largest contiguous land empire in history at its greatest extent
Loss of China to the Ming Dynasty marks major decline
Empire fully fragmented into successor khanates after Timur's death
Osman I establishes an independent principality in northwest Anatolia
Conquest of Constantinople ends the Byzantine Empire
Ottoman Empire at greatest territorial extent before the siege of Vienna
Abolition of the Ottoman sultanate following World War I
Cyrus the Great overthrows the Median Empire and establishes Persian rule
Largest empire the world had yet seen, spanning from Egypt to the Indus
Alexander the Great defeats Darius III, ending the Achaemenid dynasty
Liu Bang defeats Xiang Yu and establishes the Han Dynasty
Han Dynasty at greatest extent with control of the Silk Road
End of the Han Dynasty leading to the Three Kingdoms period
Constantine moves capital to Constantinople, founding the Eastern Roman Empire
Justinian reconquers former Western Roman territories
Fourth Crusade sacks Constantinople, fragmenting the empire
Fall of Constantinople to the Ottomans ends the Byzantine Empire
